instruction: Make an order for two same-colored Nordstrom Signature Cashmere Sweater in extra-small size on Amazon. My color preference is, yellow > orange > navy blue. Pick the most preferred color that is available.
notes: Single-app Amazon purchase task. Three product objects model the extra-small sweater variants (yellow/orange/navy blue). Runtime availability cannot be known before any API call, so it is not in :init; instead the color preference is enforced structurally: a color may only be searched once every more-preferred color has been searched ((may-search yellow) initially; each search unlocks the next color via next-preferred-color; no-fallback-color is a terminal marker with no variant). amazon.show_product on the found variant stands for the availability check; add_product_to_cart requires it. The shortest plan is the optimistic path (yellow found and in stock); if at runtime yellow (or orange) is unavailable, the agent continues with the next color, which is also a valid plan in this model. add_product_to_cart uses quantity=2 and clear_cart_first=true so the new order contains exactly one item line with quantity 2 (CartEntry changes are ignored by the evaluation). Payment card and address ids are looked up with show_payment_cards/show_addresses (no address is created or modified). Order confirmation emails/receipt files are side effects of place_order and need no extra actions. Goal: one order containing 2 units of an extra-small sweater of the most preferred available color, then complete_task with no answer.
